title: BluePeak Health - Private Network POC: success criteria & benchmarks
next_steps: Alex to send pilot contract and pricing sheet
Priya to share benchmark harness and synthetic traffic spec
BluePeak to provide sample traffic dump and VPC contact details
action_items: Priya - share benchmark script + container image - due 2026-04-02
Alex - draft pilot SOW + pricing - due 2026-04-05
Samir - share traffic histogram and VPC admin contact - due 2026-04-03
Lena - provide list of compliance docs needed (SOC2/ISO) - due 2026-04-07
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week private-network POC. Focus on residency, peering vs PrivateLink tradeoffs, benchmarks for p95 latency and throughput, and data egress constraints. Agreed next steps around benchmark artifacts, pilot SOW, and traffic samples.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call - Alex from Redwood, Priya and Marco also here. Samir, Lena, Ruth, Victor from BluePeak?
[00:00:20] Samir (BluePeak): Yep that's us. Thanks Alex. Goal for today is to scope the private network POC — we need clarity on success criteria, region/residency and how we keep egress locked down.
[00:00:40] Priya (SE): Great. We'll walk through recommended topologies (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), what we need from your side for sizing, then benchmark targets. We'll also talk timelines — typical pilot has a 6 week cadence.
[00:01:05] Victor (Product): To be explicit: success means we can push a prod-like workload through Redwood Private in our AWS account, see < 200ms p95 for our common 256-token request, and no traffic egress to non-approved regions. Also we need audit logs and KMS integration.
[00:01:30] Priya (SE): Understood. Quick qualification Qs: what's your expected QPS and token distribution? Also any long sequences (like >1024 tokens) we should plan for?
[00:01:55] Ruth (SRE): Current spike QPS is around 35 QPS, average about 12 QPS. Most requests are short — median 120 tokens, 90% under 512, but we have an analytics path that can reach ~1k tokens for batch jobs once a day.
[00:02:20] Samir (Platform): We plan for eventual multi-region control plane, but initial pilot should be single-region us-east-1. Data residency requirement: must not leave us-east-1. Egress to third-party monitoring endpoints may be okay if routed via our approved VPC endpoints only.
[00:02:45] Priya (SE): Good. For single-region us-east-1 we can do either VPC Peering (classic) or PrivateLink. Tradeoffs: peering is simpler for high-throughput but needs route table config and can require more cross-account setup; PrivateLink (Interface endpoints) gives tighter egress control and endpoint-level policies but has per-ENI overhead and sometimes slight latency increase.
[00:03:20] Marco (Solutions Eng): To add, with peering you can avoid NAT hops for large payloads; with PrivateLink you pay per ENI and there are limits on concurrent flows per endpoint. For 35 QPS with average 120 tokens, both are viable; if you scale toward hundreds QPS we recommend peering for cost/throughput.
[00:03:50] Lena (InfoSec): For compliance we need SAML SSO for console access, KMS for key control, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and a contractual guarantee that logs are retained for 1 year. Also SOC2 type II and ISO27001 docs.
[00:04:15] Alex (AE): We can provide SOC2/ISO paperwork, SSO integrations, and audit log streaming. KMS integration is supported in Redwood Private — you'll maintain your keys, and we encrypt at rest with customer-managed keys.
[00:04:40] Victor (Product): On the metrics, can you be more specific about benchmark targets we should test? p50, p95, p99? Also throughput and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:05:05] Priya (SE): For the pilot we'll propose these targets: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 150ms for 256-token requests; p95 < 400ms for 1k token batch jobs. Throughput target: sustain 60 QPS at 95% of requests' perf targets with autoscaling. Cost estimates we'll send in the pricing SOW — we'll model both Dedicated and Private options.
[00:05:40] Samir (BluePeak): What's the expected GPU type or instance blueprint inside Redwood Private for these benchmarks? We want to know if results reflect e.g., A10G/A100p4/etc.
[00:06:00] Marco (Solutions Eng): We'll run benchmarks on a config that matches our hosted profile: mixed inference nodes (A10G-like), and we'll also show a quantized 4-bit path to highlight cost/latency tradeoffs. We'll annotate every benchmark with the instance class and model variant.
[00:06:25] Ruth (SRE): On the network side, do we need to open ports inbound? Our security team is strict — prefer minimal exposure.
[00:06:40] Priya (SE): For PrivateLink you create an interface endpoint in your VPC; traffic goes over your AZ-local ENIs — no inbound open ports to public internet required. For peering you'll need proper route table entries and possibly NAT or egress proxy if your subnets are private. We'll provide a runbook.
[00:07:05] Lena (InfoSec): Auditability question: can we see per-request metadata (model version, config, token counts) in the audit logs? Need to show provenance for outputs.
[00:07:25] Alex (AE): Yes, Redwood's console exports token-level and request-level metadata; for Private we can stream logs to your S3 or SIEM with the necessary fields. We'll confirm exact schema in docs.
[00:07:45] Victor (Product): Benchmarks — can you run our real traffic shape instead of synthetic? Synthetic is fine for initial runs but we need realistic tail behavior.
[00:08:05] Priya (SE): Absolutely. Action plan: you provide sample traffic or a histogram and we'll replay it in the harness. If you prefer not to share raw content, you can provide anonymized metadata with token counts and payload sizes.
[00:08:30] Samir (BluePeak): We'll share a scrubbed sample. Also — egress restrictions — we have a hard rule: no egress outside us-east-1. How do you enforce that for calls that might go to Redwood control plane or telemetry?
[00:08:55] Marco (Solutions Eng): The control plane can be decoupled; compute in your region, control plane can be colocated or use an accept-only endpoint. For telemetry we support routing telemetry via your VPC endpoints or a collector you run. We'll document the exact endpoints and allow-list.
[00:09:20] Lena (InfoSec): We also need data usage guarantees — like no model tuning on customer data unless we opt in. That's a legal / procurement ask.
[00:09:35] Alex (AE): Noted — by default Redwood Private does not use customer data to tune shared models. We'll put that in the pilot SOW and standard contract language.
[00:09:50] Ruth (SRE): On sizing: what's the estimated disk/FS for KV cache if we have long-lived sessions? Some of our flows are chatty with KV cache hits.
[00:10:10] Priya (SE): KV cache sizing maps to concurrent sessions * avg KV footprint per session. For chatty sessions with 1k tokens average conversation, estimate about 60–80KB per active session. For your expected concurrency (~50 active sessions at peak) that's under 5MB — trivial. If concurrency grows to thousands we'll size accordingly.
[00:10:40] Victor (Product): Who's the right contact for the AWS/VPC team? We need a single point to exchange peering/private link setup steps.
[00:10:55] Samir: That's me, Samir Patel — I'll be the VPC owner. I'll share an email and the team alias.
[00:11:10] Priya (SE): Great. Bench run plan: stage 1 synthetic smoke tests for baseline, stage 2 replay of scrubbed production traffic, stage 3 stress to target autoscaling and failure modes. We'll collect p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, and token cost metrics.
[00:11:35] Marco (Solutions Eng): We'll also instrument tracing to measure KV cache hit rates and per-request cost breakdown so you can see where tokens are spent.
[00:11:50] Lena (InfoSec): For PrivateLink we need to understand the availability implications — if an AZ goes down, how does failover work? ENI limits per AZ also concern us.
[00:12:10] Marco: With Private we recommend multi-AZ endpoints for HA. ENI limits are AWS account soft-limits; we'll advise on ENI planning and fallback to cross-AZ routing via peered subnets if needed. We'll include recommended quotas in the runbook.
[00:12:35] Alex (AE): Rough timeline proposal: by 2026-04-02 Redwood shares benchmark harness; by 2026-04-05 pilot SOW and pricing; pilot kickoff 2026-04-12; 3 weeks of benchmarking + one week of validation + 2 weeks remediation and signoff = 6 weeks, target signoff end of May.
[00:13:05] Victor (Product): That timeline works but we'll confirm resource availability internally.
[00:13:20] Priya (SE): Quick note on cost tradeoffs: Dedicated GPU pools in Redwood Dedicated give predictable latency at higher cost; Redwood Private in your VPC lets you control networking and key management but cost varies based on instance choices. We will provide a cost model for both.
[00:13:45] Samir (BluePeak): Any limitations with model variants? We want to run both a 7B open model and a 33B variant for certain analytics.
[00:14:05] Priya (SE): Both are supported; larger models will obviously increase latency and memory footprint. We'll benchmark both. For 33B we may suggest batching adjustments and a larger node class.
[00:14:25] Victor (Product): On security: SAML + RBAC, and idempotent API keys? Also need rotation schedules.
[00:14:45] Alex (AE): Yes, SAML SSO, RBAC and API key rotation is supported; we also have short-lived tokens for service accounts. We'll capture the rotation cadence in the SOW.
[00:15:05] Ruth (SRE): For metrics we want Prometheus-compatible endpoints. Can we push metrics to our Prometheus or do you provide a scrape target?
[00:15:25] Marco (Solutions Eng): We can push metrics to your metric ingest or expose scrape endpoints within your VPC. We'll coordinate with your SRE to choose the path.
[00:15:45] Lena (InfoSec): DPI/inspection: can traffic be routed through our inspection appliances? Required for some regulated pipelines.
[00:16:05] Priya (SE): Yes, with peering you can route through inspection appliances. With PrivateLink you'd place inspection before or after the interface endpoint depending on architecture. We'll include a reference topology with examples.
[00:16:30] Samir (BluePeak): Ok, are there common gotchas we should watch for during setup?
[00:16:45] Marco (Solutions Eng): Common: route table misconfigs, ENI IP exhaustion in small subnets, and VPC endpoint security groups that block flows. Also, DNS resolution for interface endpoints must be configured if you want the logical hostnames to map to private addresses.
[00:17:10] Victor (Product): Can we get a post-pilot runbook for production rollout? We want recommendations for autoscaling, rollback policies, and fallback to hosted if there's an outage.
[00:17:30] Alex (AE): Yes, Redwood provides a rollout checklist: canary deploy steps, A/B traffic splitting, fallback to hosted rigs (if agreed) and monitoring thresholds. We'll include that in the SOW artifacts.
[00:17:50] Priya (SE): Quick example benchmark target we'll run in week 1: 1000 synthetic requests at 30 QPS with 256 tokens; measure p95. We'll attach the harness. If your p95 exceeds 150ms we'll iterate settings: increase instance class, change batch size, or enable a quantized path.
[00:18:20] Samir (BluePeak): How do you measure token accounting? We need to reconcile cost estimates with our billing.
[00:18:35] Marco (Solutions Eng): We emit token counts per request in logs; the billing model maps to tokens and model variant. We'll provide a sample billing spreadsheet and per-route cost calculators.
[00:18:55] Victor (Product): Any constraints around on-prem? Future ask possibly but not for this pilot.
[00:19:10] Priya (SE): On-prem is supported via our Private package; hardware procurement and network isolation steps add lead time. For now, in-cloud is faster.
[00:19:30] Lena (InfoSec): Also need SLAs for failover and RTO/RPO for critical path.
[00:19:45] Alex (AE): We'll propose SLA language in the enterprise addendum; pilot won't carry the full enterprise SLA but we'll show metrics and a plan for ramping into SLA-backed Dedicated contracts.
[00:20:05] Samir (BluePeak): Anything else from Redwood side?
[00:20:15] Priya (SE): We'll include a short checklist of required IAM roles and minimal terraform snippets to create endpoints/peering. That should speed setup.
[00:20:35] Ruth (SRE): Sounds good. We'll aim to provide scrubbed sample traffic and VPC contacts by 2026-04-03.
[00:20:50] Alex (AE): Great — recap of next steps: Priya shares benchmark harness (due 4/2), Alex sends SOW/pricing (due 4/5), BluePeak sends traffic + VPC contact (due 4/3), pilot kickoff week of 4/12. We'll put calendar invite after the call.
[00:21:15] Victor (Product): Thanks everyone.
[00:21:20] Samir (BluePeak): Thanks — look forward to the harness.
[00:21:25] Alex (AE): End of call.
